Choose a slide, try its steps, and read the **exact Markdown alongside the preview**.
Switch to **Presenter with notes** to see what the speaker receives from that
same source. This page teaches authoring; [Compare themes](compare.qmd) shows
how the same content looks in different themes.

```{=html}

      <span id="example-copy-status" role="status"></span>
```

## What to try

| Choose this slide | Try this |
|---|---|
| [Importance and footnotes](example.qmd?slide=3) | Compare `.key` and `.aside` roles and follow the footnote's return arrow. |
| [Dim layering](example.qmd?slide=4) | Advance four times. Future spans and list items stay hidden; earlier points dim. |
| [Code with an explanation](example.qmd?slide=5) | Each reveal colors its line number and explanation; a fourth advance clears dimming for the overview. Previous restores the last highlight. |
| [A stepped equation](example.qmd?slide=6) | Reveal the mean, total and count in turn; the fourth advance restores all three colored pairs to full strength on the same slide. |
| [Speaker notes](example.qmd?slide=8) | Switch between Audience and Presenter to see how one source produces two views. |
| [The appendix](example.qmd?slide=10) | Follow “The supporting data,” visit the detail slide, then return. The Markdown follows your navigation. |

## Use it in your own talk {#edit-the-source}

Follow [Start a deck](quickstart.qmd) to create your own file using a bundled
theme. Copy a slide above when you need its pattern, then replace its content.
See [Semantic slides](semantic-authoring.md) for the exact syntax rules.

The complete editable example includes twelve slides and their speaker cues.
Save the Markdown as `index.qmd`, its stylesheet as `source.css`, and the SVG
as `assets/two-views.svg`:

```{=html}
<p class="download-links"><a href="_generated/source/index.qmd.txt" download="index.qmd">Download complete Markdown</a> · <a href="_generated/source/source.css.txt" download="source.css">Download example stylesheet</a> · <a href="_generated/source/two-views.svg" download="two-views.svg">Download SVG</a></p>
```

The stylesheet supplies this example's spacing; your first deck can use the
bundled theme directly. The source and presenter output include speaking cues;
share the audience output when those cues should stay private. Audience and
presenter windows navigate independently.
